column1: 354859|complete|For every epsilon>0, eventually every linear 3-graph avoiding the six-edge 3x3 grid has at most epsilon n^2 edges.|The literal itself reports a positive-density refutation; no credit on that report alone and no independent construction replay. A grid-free dense family, not a small isolated graph, is needed.

355072|definition-dependent|For every integer m>=1 the displayed projection-constant identity is asserted; lambda_C is not defined.|Maximal ETF existence in every dimension is the substantive obstacle. Listed dimensions are instances, not an all-dimension construction.

355166|scope-ambiguous|For every m>=4, suffix permutation and length n, alternating involution avoidance counts coincide; up-down versus down-up convention is unspecified.|A suffix-uniform bijection must preserve involution and alternating orientation. Ordinary Wilf equivalence supplies neither constraint; no such map established.

355339|definition-dependent|For every n>=0 six progression congruences are asserted; elongated diamonds and link-adding operation are not defined.|A generating product and modular certificate could qualify technically, but cannot compute the literal sequence from this record alone; parameter checks would not prove all n.

355421|complete|Every essentially 4-edge-connected pseudo 2-factor isomorphic cubic bipartite graph belongs to three named finite graphs.|The literal already reports a 30-vertex counterexample. Reconstructing that known graph is not discovery; counterexample properties were not independently replayed here.

355497|scope-ambiguous|For every pair of imaginary quadratic fields the sector-prime ratio tends to inverse class-number ratio; factors in a cone are not specified for nonprincipal prime ideals.|Prime ideals versus principal generators and units affect the count. Hecke equidistribution is a strong classical-adaptation objection, not an audited bridge.

355556|definition-dependent|For every n>=0 a bijection from 201-avoiding ascent sequences to 312-machine sortable permutations is asserted; ascent sequences are undefined.|The defined stack condition helps, but an all-length bijection needs recursive states on both sides. Numerical count equality would be insufficient.

355558|definition-dependent|For every n>=1 three Fishburn-avoidance counts equal 2^n-n; Fishburn permutations are undefined.|An insertion recurrence giving a(n)=2a(n-1)+n-2 could prove the numbers, but no closed insertion state system is supplied.

355560|definition-dependent|For every n>=1 a Fishburn avoidance class equals a classical avoidance count; Fishburn restriction is undefined.|Requires a bijection or matching generating trees preserving both forbidden patterns; ordinary-class enumeration alone cannot supply the left side.

355561|definition-dependent|For every n>=0 two avoidance counts coincide; the Fishburn condition is missing.|Related ascent-sequence interpretations do not establish an exact map from this left-hand class. No full recurrence established.

355562|definition-dependent|For every n>=0 Fishburn avoidance of 1243 and 3124 matches classical avoidance of 231 and 4123; Fishburn is undefined.|A common right-hand class with 355560 does not prove equality between the two left-hand classes. Needs an independent structural bridge.

355563|definition-dependent|For every n>=1 two Fishburn classes equal the stated Catalan-binomial sum; Fishburn is undefined.|Decomposition into Catalan pieces is a possible mechanism, but an invertible decomposition and compatibility with both forbidden sets are unproved.

355564|definition-dependent|For every n>=1 indecomposable Fishburn counts equal a length n-1 classical class; Fishburn and indecomposability convention are missing.|Reported generating-function equivalence to 355563 is not verified. It cannot receive separate family credit; no decomposition proof here.

355821|definition-dependent|For every real singularity of type J10^3 and every versal deformation the real discriminant complement has exactly 33 components; type is undefined.|Constructed components give only one side. Completeness needs realization and exclusion of additional components, not a small enumeration of virtual components.

355884|definition-dependent|For every prime power q>=3 the associated ovoid code is P- and S-optimal; code construction and optimality measures are absent.|Even the cited q=5 case requires excluding a [127,8,45]_5 code. No all-q bound or full-scope certificate identified.

355983|definition-dependent|For every odd k>=3 and prime power q>=4, girth D(k,q)=k+5; adjacency equations of D(k,q) are absent.|Needs a cycle of the exact length uniformly in two parameters plus the established lower bound. A few cycles would only give instances.

356042|incomplete|Five table-defined configurations and their numerical density targets are not present.|Cannot recover the actual five assertions without the table. Near-equality of numerical flag-algebra bounds proves no exact equality.

356050|incomplete|For all prime powers q>=5 corresponding orbit counts of Theorem 2 should hold; neither action nor target counts are supplied.|The theorem is the missing proposition, not mere notation. No count can be certified from this literal.

356051|incomplete|For every m>=1 formulas in Example 6 are asserted; orbit definitions and two target formulas are absent.|The displayed t_q expression yields -1/16 at m=1 as printed, signaling missing conditions or transcription. This is a scope defect, not credit.

356096|incomplete|For every admissible prime and transfer system a derived triple should lift back; the triple and lifting procedure are omitted.|No executable construction can be checked without the subgroup-data maps. General N-infinity operad language is not a full route.

356144|complete|There exists an infinite nested insertion chain of square-free 4-letter words, each extendable at every position.|König's lemma would require arbitrarily deep compatible chains in a finitely branching tree. Independent long words need not supply such chains; no uniform extension mechanism found.

356229|complete|For every m>=3,n>=1 classical 2134...m-avoiders with peak-free inverse satisfy the finite binomial sum.|Primary v1 uses consecutive avoidance, while the literal explicitly says classical. Bounded comparison executed; restoring source scope is not discovery. No source-conjecture proof claimed.

356331|definition-dependent|For every prime p=3 mod4 the class-number congruence holds modulo32; Psi is undefined.|The modulo16 theorem cannot be lifted by congruence arithmetic alone. Need parity of the quotient error, which is not available here.

356346|scope-ambiguous|For every variable count m some Delta(m) detects regularity of all linear equations in m variables; coefficient domain and inhomogeneous convention are unspecified.|The full claim requires a uniform bound over coefficients. A bound for three homogeneous variables is only a parameter subcase.

356365|scope-ambiguous|Every D-optimal parameter set has a difference family over some abelian group of order v; admissibility appears defined using existence itself.|Distinguish numerical D-optimal conditions from actual difference-family parameters. Construction for 85 or 99 is not the universal theorem.

356368|definition-dependent|For every n>=1 two identities for recursively constructed X,Y hold; recursion is absent.|The literal reports both proved with Walnut. No new proof claim; automata and their verification certificates not inspected.

356554|complete|For every finite insoluble G and every x, the cyclic normalizer order divides the solubilizer cardinality.|Normalizer conjugation preserves the solubilizer but need not act freely. Orbit-stabilizer alone gives no divisibility; no tractable counterexample mechanism established.

356594|definition-dependent|For n>=5,n=0 or5 mod6 with k=floor((n+2)/6), a conditional graph deletion claim holds for every vertex; graph and minimal-prime property missing.|Universal deletion needs structural proof for the whole graph family. Checking n<=100 is not a full route.

356682|complete|For every planar convex domain the second Neumann eigenvalue times squared perimeter is at most16pi^2.|A variational comparison must work uniformly for arbitrary convex boundaries. Squares and equilateral triangles are equality instances, not a general proof.

356880|definition-dependent|For all positive-degree virtual complex characters, regular invertibility iff preorder minimality; regular invertibility is undefined.|Literal reports counterexamples in two finite groups. Neither character tables nor inversion notion checked; rebuilding known examples earns no credit.

357317|definition-dependent|For every n>=0 and prime q seven colored-overpartition congruences hold; overpartition convention is not defined in the literal.|Primary Conjecture1 and generating product checked. Low-degree coefficients executed for selected q only; a uniform mod32 argument and successor-body clearance remain absent.

357360|incomplete|For every one of fifteen unnamed sporadic sequences and all primes p>=5,n,r>=1 the supercongruence holds; actual sequences are absent.|Labels B,C,E,F,s18 do not define fifteen integer sequences. Cannot verify endpoints or a uniform p-adic mechanism.

357374|definition-dependent|For each i=1..12 the two KSS elliptic fibrations share their relative Jacobian; twelve pairs are not defined.|Literal says the abstract reports proof. This is a resolution lead, not proof-body qualification; no independent geometric proof audit.

357429|definition-dependent|For all 1<=k<=d and arrangements with the stated sizes suitable subspace, point and simultaneous partitions have RD>=1; RD is undefined.|The joint Tverberg-type quantifiers prevent separate per-arrangement solutions from sufficing. No all-r_i construction identified.

357494|definition-dependent|For every finite signed measure b and H in(0,1/2) strong uniqueness and existence hold; meaning of measure drift solution omitted.|Requires distributional/local-time interpretation, not pointwise b(X). Existing small-H threshold does not extend by a formal interpolation.

357511|definition-dependent|For every even n the Bender-Knuth group on linear extensions of Z_n is symmetric; group action generators omitted.|Transitivity alone is insufficient; would need a transposition and primitivity or exact generation. Small even n computations cannot establish all n.

357657|definition-dependent|For every even r>=4 some rank-r signotope is not 2-extendable; signotope axioms and extension incidence missing.|A rank-raising construction preserving obstruction could work, but finite ranks4..12 supply no general lifting proof.

357705|definition-dependent|For all positive A,B,C,D with A>=D and mixed-sign differences, x=y iff stated divisibility criterion; graph monoid undefined in literal.|Primary Definition11 restores relations. A six-step common-expansion certificate for (3,1,1,3) contradicts the displayed literal but violates the source-context nonredundancy condition A+B!=C+D. Exclude as scope correction; no proposal.

357780|definition-dependent|For every tree T, optimal Sweller-first competition-independence length >=3n/7; game rules missing.|Literal reports an arbitrarily large counterexample family. Comparing (5n+26)/12<3n/7 requires n>182; construction body not replayed.

357937|incomplete|For every irrational parameter satisfying Lemma84 and every fixed M, an O(N) bound is uniform in M; lemma, observables and sum definition omitted.|Cannot determine whether uniformity applies to N thresholds or constants. A bounded-observable trivial bound is not justified without definitions.

358034|definition-dependent|Every cyclically4-connected cubic graph on2ell+2>=8 vertices has doubled Martin invariant at least prism value, uniquely; invariant undefined.|Needs a monotonicity or surgery inequality with strict equality classification. Exhaustive graphs through20 vertices do not prove all ell.

358085|definition-dependent|There exists one bounding function for dimension by standard-example number for every cover-planar poset; standard-example number undefined.|Unbounded dimension alone is no counterexample: standard-example number must remain bounded. No such family or controlling function constructed.

358100|complete|For every prime p, maximal ternary cyclotomic height with least prime p is <=2p/3.|Literal reports the bound proved. Original Beiter refutation is a different bound and must not be confused with this one; source proof not audited.

358184|complete|For every integer n>=11 the sextic binomial truncation has Galois group S6.|Finite factorization or discriminant tests cannot eliminate the infinite exceptional set. Needs uniform local ramification/irreducibility argument; no short full-scope route identified.

358375|definition-dependent|For each d normalized cusp polynomial has positivity and irreducibility, every integer specialization m!=-1 irreducible and stated m=-1 factorization; NH_d missing.|Several universal clauses need separate checks including zero/unit conventions. Finite d<=30 factorization offers no irreducibility mechanism for all specializations.

358392|incomplete|For every t in unspecified T minus explicit T1, unspecified graph has five 5-cycles.|Missing T and graph construction prevent evaluating even one new parameter. Exceptional list alone is not an effective proposition.

358423|definition-dependent|For every n>=11 there is an h-convex K_n drawing with all edges crossed; h-convexity undefined.|Cloning vertices might preserve crossings but requires hereditary convex-side consistency. No verified all-n extension operation established.

358567|incomplete|For every beta<min(x^-1,y) a source-defined implicit curve is well-defined and a random-partition limit; curve, measure and parameter domain absent.|Cannot define convergence or positive probability from the literal. Restoring a signed/nonpositive regime needs source work, not an immediate contradiction.

358658|definition-dependent|For every f in undefined S_G^* and every n>=2 sharp abs(a_n)<=1/(2(n-1)); n6 highlighted.|A sixth-coefficient extremization would leave the all-n assertion unproved. Need a class-specific generating/subordination mechanism before calculation.

358758|complete|For every permutation length the listed S4 patterns have precisely the five non-singleton descent-bottom distribution equivalence classes.|Finite lengths can separate pairs but cannot prove any positive equivalence for all lengths. Reverse-complement transfers a proved Destop classification only if that classification is itself proved; not established here.
